en: The Triplet of the Wholesome (Kusalattika) and the Dyad of the Visible (Sanidassanaduka)
An indeterminate visible phenomenon is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an indeterminate non-visible phenomenon.
An indeterminate visible phenomenon [is a condition] for a wholesome non-visible phenomenon... [and so on]. (Six questions are to be formulated. In the case of the object-condition there are six;

in the case of the predominance-condition, three; in the case of the decisive support-condition and the prenascence-condition, six; in the case of the presence-condition and the non-disappearance-condition, six.

Dependent on a wholesome, non-demonstrable state, a state that is neither wholesome nor non-demonstrable arises by way of root condition. With the unwholesome, there are three; with the indeterminate, there are three. Under root condition there are nine … pe … under result condition there are three … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are nine.
